clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952 and the purchase of the orchard, within eighteen months: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, her distance from Walter as he worked long hours, Glen's fights at school, June's weeks in bed through the winter, Walter's cutoff from his brother Harlan over their father's land money, rows between Walter and June over money for new trees, and June's joining the church choir and easing of her homesickness by September 1953. Glen's stomach aches are noted but undated to a year, so they are not linked. The shifts pile up as the family settled into the valley, with Walter absorbed in the orchard, June grieving the distance from her sister, and Glen struggling at his new school.

clusters.name: The orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter's heavy drinking, his and Glen's blame of each other over the loan, the sale of the orchard at auction in October and the move to Ridgeport, Glen and Marian's overfunctioning as they took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's worsening asthma that winter, Nora's bed-wetting in April 1969, and Ida's heart trouble found that May. Walter's functioning rose in October 1969 when he stopped drinking and took work pruning trees, closing the period. The shifts show the family's reactions spreading from Walter's drinking and the conflict with Glen through the household and to the extended family.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975 when the Ridgeport cannery closed: Glen's months out of work sitting in the truck in the yard, loud fights between Glen and Marian over money at night, Marian's taking a second job cleaning offices, Nora's loss of appetite and weight loss through the summer, her distance from Marian, Walter's return to heavy drinking in December, and Nora's eating again and making the track team by June 1976. Glen began driving a delivery truck for the feed store in March 1976. The shifts show the family's reactions spreading from Glen's loss through the household and to Nora and Walter.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Sam's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into Nora and Sam's house in January 1990: clashes between Nora and Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals, Sam's distance from Nora as he kept out of the kitchen rows, his turning toward his mother, Owen's tantrums at preschool, Wilma's taking over Lily's care, Nora's eczema flaring on both hands, rows between Nora and Sam most nights, and Marian driving over twice a week to take Nora's side. Wilma took a flat in town in June 1991, and Nora's eczema cleared over the summer, closing the period. The shifts show conflict spreading through the household as Wilma's presence realigned the family.
